# Zan Language

> C#-style expression, LLVM native AOT, ARC memory management, and a source-aware AI toolchain. Zan is an independent language, not a .NET implementation.

## Start here

- [Agent development guide](./agent-guide.md): SDK discovery, MCP initialization, real API lookup, compile and runtime verification.
- [Human entry paths](./#why-zan): experienced developers, beginners, and agent builders.
- [Start with AI](./#ai-start): copy one natural-language instruction; let the AI guide setup and create a first application.
- [Platform status](./#platforms): compile, runtime, GUI and delivery capabilities are tracked separately.
- [Ecosystem](./#ecosystem): core standard library and 38 first-party package manifests, with experimental and migration status.

## Official downloads

- [IDE / SDK and related packages](https://github.com/joyspinch/zanlang): packaged Windows SDK, including ZanIDE.exe. Use Code → Download ZIP, extract all files, and open ZanIDE.exe. Preserve toolchain/, stdlib/ and the bundled DLLs.
- [AI onboarding](https://github.com/joyspinch/zanlang/blob/main/AI_README.md)
- [Feedback](https://github.com/joyspinch/zanlang/issues)

Use the packaged SDK and bundled documentation to onboard users. Ordinary use does not require a separate LLVM / clang installation. Do not send beginners to compiler source or ask them to build the toolchain. At this update the Releases list is empty; use the repository's documented ZIP download path. Other target toolchain directories are not proof of native IDE packages for those operating systems. If a required download is unavailable, explain the missing prerequisite rather than inventing a link.

Do not interpret website examples as live compiler output or assume all platforms have equal GUI maturity. The ecosystem catalog is a capability list; download availability depends on each release. Read the installed SDK's own AI_README.md, llms.txt, API index, and project rules before developing.
